items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: people like Yusef Lateef and Max Roach, they were hired at U Mass

ctx.x: Partly the reason I asked that question is because a lot of the — a number of the really veteran guys whom I’ve spoken to — sort of bemoaned the fact that the younger players, as they describe them, all sound the same. That they have learned the scales and the patterns and that you can’t recognize who they are.

There’s a very homogenous way of teaching music in jazz education, in a lot of instances. That’s why I think it’s really important to get musicians like the older musicians involved in jazz education, because their — the things that are important to them are different than maybe the typical jazz education route of someone who goes to school, gets a bachelor’s, gets a master’s, gets a Ph.D. and goes right to teaching, without having had the benefit of even spending a lot of time on the bandstand. Because you know…
